aiSummary: Choctawhatchee Bay is fishing well heading into early August, with speckled trout leading the inshore bite across scattered bay locations and at least one bull red topping 40 inches confirmed in the system recently. Today's conditions are favorable — light westerly wind of 0–10 mph, sunny skies, and 85°F water — though a 12% storm chance before 4 PM means early starters have the edge. Plan to be off exposed water or at least watching the horizon by mid-morning, and take advantage of the calm window to work grass flats and structure before any afternoon convection develops.

bridge.aiNote: The 331 Bridge spans the narrow neck of Choctawhatchee Bay, creating a current funnel that pushes bait through on both tides and concentrates trout, redfish, sheepshead, and black drum around the pilings year-round. The lee-side pilings are the prime ambush zone on incoming tides. Being open and exposed, this is typically the first spot to become unfishable when wind picks up.
bridge.todaysCall: With wind running W 0–10 mph today, chop at the bridge should be minimal and conditions workable, but plan your session around the low tide at 8:10 AM — current moving through the pilings early will be your best window before the water goes slack. The slight stain in the water is actually an asset here, keeping fish tucked tight to the pilings where they're easier to target. With the storm window before 4 PM, get your bridge time in early and be off open water by early afternoon. The recent trout bite across the bay makes the bridge pilings worth a serious look with soft plastics or live shrimp on the outgoing current.

alaqua.aiNote: Alaqua Bayou offers protected water with a strong year-round redfish population, along with trout and flounder near the mouth. The oyster bars at the creek mouth are the prime structure to target, and tree cover keeps water temperatures a few degrees cooler than the open bay. The upper creek transitions toward brackish and can hold bass alongside smaller reds.
alaqua.todaysCall: Today's light westerly wind and calm conditions make Alaqua's protected interior comfortable to fish, but the real draw is the shade and cooler water — that tree cover will matter with 85°F bay-wide temps and full August sun bearing down. Focus on the oyster bars at the mouth early, especially with the low tide at 8:10 AM pulling water out and concentrating bait. The slightly stained water suits redfish well; work weedless gold spoons or dark soft plastics along the bar edges. With the storm window before 4 PM, Alaqua's sheltered character also makes it one of the safer places to ride out any pop-up if you can't make it back quickly.

basin.aiNote: Basin Bayou sees less pressure than neighboring Alaqua and LaGrange, which tends to mean less-educated fish and more willing biters. The interior grass flats are classic sight-fishing territory for redfish in under two feet of water. Pompano occasionally show at the mouth on moving tides in late spring and early summer, and the bayou is less protected than LaGrange if weather builds.
basin.todaysCall: The low-pressure fishing crowd and today's calm 0–10 mph west wind make Basin Bayou an appealing option for anglers who want to sight-fish reds without competition. Low tide at 8:10 AM will concentrate fish on the interior grass flats early — get in position before first light near sunrise at 6:03 AM and be ready to sight-cast as the sun rises and visibility improves on the shallow flats. The slightly stained water will reduce sight-fishing distance, so move slowly and look for wakes and pushes rather than relying on pure visual. Given Basin is less protected than LaGrange, keep an eye on the sky ahead of the pre-4 PM storm window and have a plan to exit if clouds start stacking.

lagrange.aiNote: LaGrange Bayou is the top trout producer in this area of the bay — the oyster bars at the mouth are legendary, and interior grass flats hold redfish year-round. Deep holes inside are reliable habitat for black drum and sheepshead. It's also the most protected water on this side of the bay, making it the default choice when weather threatens.
lagrange.todaysCall: With the bay-wide speckled trout bite running strong through late July, LaGrange's storied oyster bars at the mouth should be a priority stop — work them on the outgoing tide around the 8:10 AM low with jigs or live shrimp for the best shot at quality trout. Once the tide bottoms out, transition to the interior grass flats for redfish, which should be actively feeding as the flood starts building toward the high at 10:32 PM tonight. The slightly stained water and last-quarter moon combine for moderate tidal movement — not a ripping current, but enough to get bait moving around the oysters. If any pre-4 PM storms do materialize, LaGrange is your best shelter option on this side of the bay.

fourmile.aiNote: Four Mile Creek is a tidal creek running between Shipyard Marina and the bay, with tidal flow that pushes baitfish up the creek on incoming tides and concentrates redfish and trout in the bends and grass edges. The creek mouth is a prime flounder zone, and the upper section transitions toward brackish water that can hold bass and smaller reds. It's short and protected, making it one of the safest fisheries when weather threatens.
fourmile.todaysCall: Four Mile Creek's best window today aligns with the transition off the 8:10 AM low tide — as water starts flooding back in, baitfish get pushed up into the bends and the reds and trout follow. Start at the creek mouth early for a flounder opportunity, then work your way into the bends with soft plastics or live bait as the incoming tide builds. The creek's protected nature makes it an excellent call given the 12% storm chance before 4 PM — you can fish comfortably without worrying much about deteriorating bay conditions. Light west wind today means even the creek mouth won't have much chop, so a light spinning or baitcasting setup will cover the water well.

hogtown.aiNote: Hogtown Bayou is a signature Santa Rosa Beach guide spot and one of the most consistently productive trout flats on Choctawhatchee Bay. Summer mornings are the peak window, with trout stacked on grass in two to four feet of water. Spanish mackerel show at the mouth on moving tides, and the bayou sits further from the 331 Bridge than the other spots on this dashboard — factor in run time.
hogtown.todaysCall: This is arguably the highest-percentage play for speckled trout today given the strong bay-wide bite and Hogtown's reputation as a guide-grade trout flat — plan to be on the grass in two to four feet by first light with the sunrise at 6:03 AM. The 8:10 AM low tide means the first hour or two of your session will have water pulling off the flats, concentrating trout — stay mobile and cover the edges. Slightly stained water calls for brighter or louder lures; chartreuse or red-and-white paddle tails and popping corks are solid choices. Factor in the longer run from the 331 Bridge and be off or heading in ahead of any pre-4 PM storm window — exposed water and a fast run home don't mix well when cells pop up.

mallet.aiNote: Mallet Bayou is a small tributary feeding directly into LaGrange Bayou — this dashboard's top trout producer — just south of Freeport. That direct connection makes it plausible that LaGrange's oyster-bar trout and redfish patterns extend into this smaller, quieter water, though documented fishing history here is limited. Its small, interior character likely makes it a calm-water fallback when wind picks up on the open bay.
mallet.todaysCall: With today's wind light at W 0–10 mph, conditions don't demand a wind-shelter fallback, but Mallet's quiet interior could still reward anglers looking for less competition than LaGrange's more-fished mouth. The best approach today is to treat it as an extension of the LaGrange trip — hit the LaGrange oyster bars early on the outgoing tide, then ease up into Mallet as the flood begins and fish push into the shallower water. Given the limited documentation on this spot, keep expectations calibrated and focus on working any visible structure or grass edges with soft plastics or shrimp. Pre-4 PM storm window is a non-issue here given the sheltered interior.

mack.aiNote: Mack Bayou sits on the barrier-island side of Choctawhatchee Bay near Topsail Hill Preserve State Park, well west of the 331 Bridge — this is a long-run destination, not a quick local trip. It shares the same protected bayou character as Alaqua and LaGrange, with marsh grass, oyster bars, and interior holes, and sees less pressure simply due to its distance. Hewett Bayou and Buck Bayou sit immediately to the east and are realistically fishable in the same outing.
mack.todaysCall: The commitment to run out to Mack Bayou is easier to justify today given the calm 0–10 mph west wind — flat water on the bay makes the long run manageable and safe. Plan to fish the oyster bars and grass edges on the outgoing tide early, then work the interior as water floods back in through the afternoon. Low pressure from distance means fish here haven't seen much, which is a meaningful advantage when the bay-wide bite is as active as it's been. Build in enough buffer to be off the open-water run before any pre-4 PM storm window, and pair this stop with Hewett and Buck to make the run worthwhile.

hewett.aiNote: Hewett Bayou sits immediately east of Mack Bayou on the barrier-island side of Choctawhatchee Bay near Topsail Hill Preserve State Park, making it a natural partner spot in the same trip. It offers the same protected bayou habitat as its neighbors — oyster bars and marsh grass at the mouth, deeper interior holes further in. Light pressure due to distance from the main boat ramps keeps fish relatively uneducated.
hewett.todaysCall: Like Mack Bayou to its west, Hewett is most worth the run on a calm day like today with west wind at 0–10 mph making the open-bay transit smooth. Target the oyster bars at the mouth on the outgoing morning tide around the 8:10 AM low, then follow the incoming flood into the interior for reds on grass edges. The slightly stained water favors redfish, which use scent and lateral line as much as sight — darker or chartreuse soft plastics and weedless rigs will work well in the shallows. Coordinate your departure time to beat the pre-4 PM storm window and use the run home on a still-calm bay.

buck.aiNote: Buck Bayou is the smallest and least-documented of the three neighboring bayous on the barrier-island side of Choctawhatchee Bay near Topsail Hill Preserve State Park. Its habitat should track its larger neighbors — marsh grass, some oyster structure, and a modest interior — but there's less basis for confident specific predictions. It's best approached as a bonus stop on a Mack and Hewett Bayou trip rather than a standalone destination.
buck.todaysCall: Buck's value today is as an add-on to a Mack/Hewett run, and the calm conditions make that multi-stop approach realistic. Give it 30–45 minutes of exploratory fishing — work any visible oyster structure at the mouth and poke into the interior to see if reds are using the grass edges on the tide movement. Don't over-commit here given the limited track record; if it shows fish, great, and if not, you've already fished two productive spots on the same run. Keep the pre-4 PM storm window in mind and treat Buck as your last stop before heading back across the open bay.
